quotes.text: The benchmark spans one in-domain center and three out-of-domain (OOD) centers.

rationale: Sources are named across four centers, but the packet does not report source versions or a clear public route from each benchmark task to its original source record. Pinned paper version is arxiv/2510.24654v2; no repo commit or access date is present in the packet.

quotes.text: Due to licensing restrictions, we are unable to directly open-source the dataset.

rationale: The paper reports the data origin and mentions licensing restrictions, satisfying origin plus one provenance/licence element. It does not report consent, IRB status, or an explicit not-required determination.

quotes.text: the benchmark comprises a total of 2,257 physician-validated patient cases

rationale: The benchmark reports descriptive dataset statistics and source stratification. It does not compare patient features against a named target population.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code/configuration, and S5 prompts. The packet reports clinical validity and evaluator validation, but not dedicated unsafe-output or bias tests.

quotes.text: we strictly selected case reports published after January 2025

rationale: The packet reports developer-side contamination controls, including post-January-2025 selection for PMC-OA and filtering to prevent diagnosis leakage. It does not report a canary, overlap measurement, or combined control plus measured contamination check.

quotes.text: contains no information about the final diagnosis

rationale: The paper states the agent state omits the final diagnosis, indicating isolation from the gold label. It does not name a runtime access-control mechanism such as no mount, no credentials, or no network path.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code/configuration, and S5 prompts. The packet names models and data sources, but does not pin the data, software harness commit, simulator, and judge into a frozen evaluation environment.

quotes.text: each case undergoes a rigorous review by a physician

rationale: Physician review and reference trajectories provide manual evidence that task configurations are clinically plausible. No scripted oracle solution is reported as run through the grader.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code/configuration, and S5 prompts. The benchmark includes simulated examination-order actions that update the dialogue state, but the packet does not report checks that irrelevant state remains unchanged.

quotes.text: computing precision, recall, and F1-score to measure recommendation quality

rationale: The benchmark design compares recommended exams with reference trajectories and diagnoses, making arbitrary outputs less likely to score well. It does not report empirical random or trivial-agent success rates.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code/configuration, and S5 prompts. The packet reports many LLM and agentic baselines, but no do-nothing or random-agent result.

quotes.text: the LLM judge demonstrated high reliability across all metrics

rationale: The paper validates its own automated evaluator against physician consensus and reports agreement/error figures. Supplementary Table 1 includes numerical agreement and MAE values.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code/configuration, and S5 prompts. S1-S3 do not state seeds or temperature-zero safeguards plus a repeated-run policy for the harness.
Headline comparisons report 95% confidence intervals and statistical significance markings. This satisfies CI or test reporting for model comparisons.

quotes.text: We consistently apply a zero-shot prompting strategy across all models.

rationale: The paper reports a sampling/prompting policy, but not the number of independent runs behind each headline score. Independence of runs is not stated.

quotes.text: All metrics are reported with 95% Confidence Intervals

rationale: Headline score tables include 95% confidence intervals. The packet does not state the resampling or variance unit or address clustering within patients/templates.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code/configuration, and S5 prompts. No identical rerun action agreement, final-state agreement, pass^k, or score-level rerun variance is reported.
Some exact model identifiers and dated snapshots are reported. Decoding parameters for reported results and the harness version or commit are not reported in S1-S3.

quotes.text: Based on the patient's initial presentation, the following investigation(s) should be performed: [one additional test]

rationale: The benchmark uses a text-command protocol for requesting examinations, so A5 is not NA. The agent-visible prompt specifies the examination-request action, but there is no machine-readable schema for every tool and no documented error/failure return semantics.

quotes.text: predict the most likely results for a specific medical examination

rationale: The packet discloses simulated examination-result behavior, and that behavior reaches agent-visible prompting. It does not report conformance tests showing the tool contract behaves as documented.

quotes.text: all returned examination results are simulated by the DiagGym

rationale: The benchmark identifies examination recommendations as clinical actions and states that returned results are simulated. It also scores examination quality and efficiency through F1/reward components and turn penalties.

The paper names grader inputs and use of LLM judgement, and justifies rubric-based judging as a complement to automated metrics. It validates against human labels, but does not provide per-class error rates for injected correct and incorrect outcomes.

quotes.text: This step removes instances where the model may have inadvertently introduced the final diagnosis

rationale: The packet reports leakage controls and train/test held-out construction. It does not report canaries or provenance markers on released tasks.

quotes.text: The benchmark spans one in-domain center and three out-of-domain (OOD) centers.

rationale: Results are reported by benchmark axis/source, and slice sizes are reported for those data sources. No patient demographic subgroup results are reported, despite clinical source data plausibly containing demographic fields.

quotes.text: Researchers with valid [CITI certification](https://physionet.org/content/mimiciv/view-required-training/3.1/#1) may also contact the authors directly

rationale: The environment-state source is stated as EHR-derived and benchmark data includes synthetic DDXPlus among real/mixed sources. Governance and redistribution terms are separately discussed through licensing restrictions, PhysioNet plans, and CITI certification access.
